tool.name: MsQuality
tool.description: calculate standardized quality metrics for mass spectrometry data

source('${__tool_directory__}/msquality_wrapper.R')
# Sample labels are taken from the input element identifiers, the metrics are # reported under these labels and the mzQC documents are named after them. input_files <- c() #for $f in $input input_files['${f.element_identifier}'] <- '${f}' #end for
metrics <- c() #if str($metric_selection.mode) == 'select' #for $m in $metric_selection.metrics metrics <- c(metrics, '${m}') #end for #end if
run_msquality( input_files = input_files, metrics = metrics, #if str($output_format) == 'tabular' out_metrics = 'metrics.tsv', out_legend = 'metrics_legend.tsv', #end if #if str($output_format) == 'mzqc' mzqc_dir = 'mzqc', #end if #if str($generate_plots).lower() == 'true' plots_dir = 'plots', #end if ms_level = ${ms_level}L, #if str($filter_empty).lower() == 'true' filter_empty = TRUE, #else filter_empty = FALSE, #end if cores = suppressWarnings(max(1L, as.integer(Sys.getenv("GALAXY_SLOTS")), na.rm = TRUE)) )

param.name: input
param.label: Input files
param.help: One or more mzML files. Every file is treated as one sample, so pass the whole measurement series to compare samples.

param.name: metrics
param.label: Metrics
param.help: Metrics marked as needing MS2 precursor data return no value for MS1-only files.

param.name: output_format
param.label: Report metrics as
param.option: Tabular file (one row per sample, all metrics)
mzQC (one document per sample, as a list collection)
param.help: MzQC only contains the metrics covered by the HUPO-PSI controlled vocabulary and writes one document per sample. The tabular file always reports every calculated metric.

param.name: generate_plots
param.label: Plot the calculated metrics
param.help: Creates one plot per metric as a list collection.

param.name: filter_empty
param.label: Remove empty and zero intensity spectra before calculating
param.help: Matching the way QuaMeter skips spectra with no peaks, which makes the metrics comparable to that software.

tool.help:
What it does ------------
Calculates low level quality metrics for mass spectrometry data with the Bioconductor package **MsQuality**. Metrics describe properties of a single measurement, such as the chromatography duration, the number of spectra, the area under the total ion chromatogram or the retention time interquartile range, and are defined by the HUPO-PSI mzQC framework.
MsQuality needs as little information about the data as possible: retention time, m/z and intensity are read directly from the mzML files through the `Spectra` package.
Inputs ------
Pass the complete measurement series rather than single files. Every input file is calculated as one sample and the metrics of the samples are reported side by side, which is how they are meant to be read: a metric is rarely meaningful on its own, but a sample drifting away from the others is. The input element identifiers become the sample names in the output.
Outputs -------
* **Tabular file**: one row per sample, one column per metric. Metrics that return more than one value add one column per value, named after the metric (`ticQuantileRtFraction.25%`). * **Metric legend**: the PSI-MS accession of every calculated metric, so the column names can be looked up without leaving Galaxy. * **mzQC**: one document per sample, collected in a list that mirrors the input collection and named after the input samples. Only metrics covered by the HUPO-PSI controlled vocabulary are written. The documents are tagged with the `mzqc` data type where the Galaxy installation provides it. * **Plots**: one plot per calculated metric, collected in a list.
Limitations -----------
* MsQuality calculates metrics only. It does not select QC samples, does not know about batches and does not normalize or correct anything; only samples of the same type should be compared. Tools such as `proBatch` or `MatrixQCvis` cover those steps. * Metrics that depend on precursor annotations return no value for MS1 only data. They are marked in the metric list. * Some metrics can return `NaN` for very short runs, for example when there are not enough scans to compute a quantile. * Writing mzQC needs the PSI-MS controlled vocabulary. When the job has no network access, a version bundled with the `rmzqc` package is used instead; the version that was used is recorded in the mzQC document. * Every mzQC document names its input file after the input element it was made from, but records the location of the copy of that file the job read: a dataset in Galaxy has no address that outlives the job, so the location is only useful for tracing a run back, not for opening the file elsewhere.
